title: Sharp Effect Sets for Synthetic Control with Invalid Auxiliary Blocks and Record Errors
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the delivered deterministic sensitivity package incremental below the required field floor (paper-score ceiling 6.2 < 7.4), with no same-scope salvage; the three math-panel statement/dependency findings were repaired and graph-checked after the halt.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is an exact deterministic compatibility analysis conditional on externally chosen error and bridge radii; it does not calibrate those radii or establish confidence coverage

The finite-union characterization, binomial component bound with an attaining construction, fit-face criterion, and common-observation modulus are proved, but their derivations are largely finite-dimensional polyhedral geometry, which limits the contribution’s breadth and leading-journal significance.

The claimed exact certificate verifier is supplied as an exhaustive enumeration argument rather than a reproducible implementation, while the Germany computation depends on asserted exact interval evaluations that are not accompanied here by executable certificate files.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a sharp sparse-validity union, an attained binomial component bound, a common-observation modulus, and a conditional Germany sensitivity audit. D0.5 graded the delivered package incremental below the required field floor and found no same-scope salvage. Three math-panel statement/dependency defects were repaired and graph-checked after the halt; the run did not enter Lean formalization or independent executable certificate verification.
tldr: The field-level kernel is the sharp finite-union effect geometry for short-panel synthetic control with at most \(s\) invalid auxiliary blocks, heterogeneous entrywise treated and donor record-error boxes, and a separate primary postperiod bridge radius. The union has at most \(\binom K{K-s}=\binom K s\) connected components, and an explicit rational superincreasing construction attains all of them as pairwise disjoint positive-length intervals. KooGuo2026 equation (7) is exactly the \(K=0\), zero-post-error specialization; the strict extension lies in sparse-validity geometry, maximal disconnectedness, weight-dependent record boxes, and the attained common-observation modulus, not in generic linear programming or the mere use of one uncertainty class. Supporting results give fit-face erasure, scale-free separation, optimal deterministic reporting radii, and proof-carrying endpoints. The Germany audit remains deterministic and conditional on external sensitivity radii, with no calibrated confidence, stochastic minimax, or coding-novelty claim.
gap: Multiple-outcome synthetic controls exploit shared structure, FermanPinto2021 studies estimator bias from imperfect pretreatment fit in a factor-model asymptotic regime, Powell2026 modifies noisy synthetic-control moments under known validity structure, and existing sensitivity analyses vary weights inside one uncertainty class. These lines do not characterize the joint effect of an adversarial unknown invalid-block budget and heterogeneous bounded record error, where the admissible class is a nonconvex finite union and donor errors depend on the candidate weights.
fill: The two headline theorems give the sharp finite union with an exact disconnected rational witness and the attained common-observation two-world modulus. Supporting results give the signed sign margin and its positive-case threshold, the face-relative iff test, scale-free separation, optimal reporting radii, proof-carrying endpoint records, and a pinned public-data audit.
